article.Citation/Title: Das, R. K., Gale, G., Walsh, K., Hennessy, V. E., Iskandar, G., Mordecai, L. A., Brandner, B., Kindt, M., Curran, H. V., & Kamboj, S. K. (2019). Ketamine can reduce harmful drinking by pharmacologically rewriting drinking memories. Nature Communications, 10, 5187.
article.InterventionDescription: Ketamine hydrochloride IV infusion (350 ng/ml plasma target, 30 min) or saline placebo, given 5 minutes after retrieval of alcohol-related or control memories; single session at UCL/UCLH.

article.Outcome: Methods, 'Statistical approach' explicitly names 'Primary drinking-related dependent variables (cue reactivity, alcohol consumption)', assessed with 2(Time)x3(Group) mixed ANOVA/mixed models -- these two domains are co-designated primary, with no single outcome named primary above the other. Chose alcohol consumption (not cue reactivity) as the SUD-behavioral outcome matching this review's eligibility criterion (b) (consumption quantity/frequency) and the paper's own headline claim (Abstract: 'reduced ... long-term drinking levels'; title: 'reduce harmful drinking'). Within alcohol consumption, used the RET+KET group's own reduction from baseline to post-manipulation (Results, 'Drinking behavior': 'highly significant reductions in general alcohol consumption ... F(1,89.17) = 19.55, p < 0.001, np2 = 0.14'), i.e. the active-treatment arm's effect on the primary drinking DV, rather than: (1) the larger np2 values reported for cue-reactivity simple effects (up to np2=0.219 for post-consumption urge to drink more beer), which were not chosen per the 'primary, not largest' rule; or (2) the 3-group Group x Time omnibus interaction on alcohol consumption itself, which was only marginally significant and reported without an eta-squared [F(2,89.432) = 3.123, p = 0.049] -- noted here for transparency since it is arguably the more literal 'primary comparison' test in this 3-arm design, but it supplies no partial eta squared to record as Outcome. A covariate-adjusted version of this same interaction, explicitly labelled 'the primary mixed-model analysis of unit alcohol consumption' by the authors, is reported later with np2 [F(2,85.42)=3.719, p=0.037, np2=0.078] (Results, 'Predictive blood biomarkers of response'), but this includes achieved plasma ketamine level as a post hoc covariate not part of the original 2x3 design, so it was not used as Outcome either; it is recorded here as an alternative candidate.
article.SD: F(1,89.17) = 19.55, the test statistic (with Satterthwaite-approximated df) printed in the same sentence as the np2 = 0.14 value used for Outcome (Results, 'Drinking behavior').
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Coded as 30, the number randomized to RET+KET (Methods, 'Design and procedure': 'Random allocation to the active group (RET+KET) and two control conditions (N = 30 per group)'). Flagged as an inference: the reported df_error of 89.17 for this F-test reflects the shared Satterthwaite denominator df of the joint linear mixed model fit across all three groups' longitudinal data (the article states 'linear mixed models were used to analyze follow-up data'), not the RET+KET arm's own N specifically, so the true per-arm analyzed N for this simple effect cannot be independently verified from the text; the one participant whose TLFB data were lost to technical error was in RET+PBO, not RET+KET, so 30 is used as the best-supported approximation for this arm's analyzed subgroup.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Thirteen of fourteen elements are described. Objective (Introduction/Abstract hypotheses), design (3-arm, single-blind, placebo-controlled reconsolidation-interference RCT), setting (UCL and UCLH), eligibility (AUDIT>8, non-SCID-AUD, >40/>30 units/week, beer-preferring, non-treatment-seeking), intervention (ketamine infusion protocol, dosing, timing), comparator (RET+PBO and No RET+KET arms), outcomes (cue reactivity, TLFB drinking measures), sample_size_power (G*Power a priori calculation, N=78 required vs N=90 randomized), randomization ('Random allocation ... N=30 per group'), blinding ('single-blind and placebo controlled'), statistical_methods (detailed 'Statistical approach' section), and results (extensive) are all explicitly described. Funding/COI is described (MRC grant in Acknowledgements; 'The authors declare no competing interests'). Harms is not met: the article never describes a harms-assessment method (no AE case-report form, no safety-monitoring protocol stated) nor reports any harms results (no AE counts, no statement that no AEs occurred) for this study's own participants -- Discussion only makes general, literature-level reassurances about ketamine's safety profile ('we argue are minimal', 'widely used and safe') without describing what was actually monitored or observed in this trial.

article.RandomizationYN: Explicit random allocation to three arms, N=30/group (Methods, 'Design and procedure').
article.BlindingYN: Methods, 'Design and procedure': 'Drug manipulations were single-blind and placebo controlled.'
article.Double+Blind: Explicitly single-blind, not double-blind, per the same sentence; coded 0, consistent with BlindingYN=1 (blinding was present but not double-blind, so no BlindingYN=0/Double+Blind=1 contradiction).
article.Comparator: Two control arms: RET+PBO (memory retrieval + placebo infusion, controlling for retrieval per se) and No RET+KET (ketamine after control/orange-juice memory retrieval, controlling for ketamine's non-reconsolidation effects). Both are legitimate comparison arms against the active RET+KET condition.
article.PrimaryCare: No aspect of recruitment, delivery, or follow-up interfaces with primary-care settings or providers; conducted entirely at a specialist psychopharmacology unit and hospital (UCL/UCLH). Coded 0 (absent), not 3, since the concept is straightforwardly answerable and simply did not occur.
article.Retention (%): Denominator = randomized N (90; Methods: 'we randomized N=30/group'). No separate 'enrolled' N distinct from randomized is reported. The article does not state a single overall study-completion percentage; the only explicit post-randomization completion counts given are the 9-month follow-up respondent Ns (Methods, 'Design and procedure': 'Attrition during remote follow-up left 9 month respondent Ns at: Ret+PBO=20/RET+KET=17/No RET+KET=19'). Completers = 20+17+19 = 56. Retention = 56/90 x 100 = 62.2%. Note this differs from completion of the immediate Day-1/Day-3/Day-10 in-person protocol, which the article frames separately and implies was materially more complete (the only reported deviation there is one participant's Day-10 TLFB data lost to 'technical error', not withdrawal); the Methods explicitly attach the word 'attrition' to remote follow-up specifically ('Attrition during remote follow-up'), supporting that in-person completion and follow-up completion are distinct, but only the follow-up N is directly stated, so it is used here as the best-supported study-wide retention figure.
article.MediatingYN: Coded 0, not 1: plasma ketamine/norketamine/dhNK levels were measured and correlated (Spearman) with drinking outcomes (Table 2, 'Predictive blood biomarkers of response'), and adding ketamine level as a covariate to the mixed model changed the Group x Time interaction. This is consistent with a mediating role narratively, but no formal mediation model (indirect-effect/Sobel/bootstrap test of an a*b pathway) was run — only bivariate correlations and a covariate-adjusted ANOVA term. No formal test of mediation exists, so 0 rather than 1.
article.ModeratingYN: Coded 0, not 1: no interaction term between a measured candidate moderator (e.g., sex, baseline AUDIT) and treatment group was tested. The ketamine-plasma-level covariate analysis (F(2,85.42)=3.719, p=0.037) adjusts the Group x Time interaction for a continuous covariate but is not reported as a formal covariate x Group interaction/moderation test — it is presented as variance explained by adding a covariate, not a moderation analysis. No candidate moderator x treatment interaction is reported anywhere, so 0.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Methods, 'Participants': AUDIT>8, not meeting SCID criteria for AUD at screening, consuming >40 (men) or >30 (women) UK units/week, primarily drinking beer, non-treatment seeking.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Multiple validated instruments used, including AUDIT, OCDS, SOCRATES, BAS/BIS, BDI, CEOA, DTS, PANAS, and SCID (Table 1; Methods).
article.BaseStatus: Judgment call. The sample scored very highly on drinking quantity/frequency (74.09+/-37.92 UK units/week) and AUDIT (22.13+/-4.93, described in Results as 'denoting physically harmful drinking and moderate-high risk of developing AUD'), and Discussion calls the pattern 'clearly harmful and problematic ... equivalent to that seen in clinical AUD.' However, participants explicitly 'did not meet SCID criteria for [AUD or] severe alcohol dependence at screening' and were not formally diagnosed or treatment-seeking. Coded 'Moderate' to reflect a harmful/hazardous-drinking population that is sub-diagnostic for severe dependence by the study's own SCID criterion, rather than 'Severe' (no formal severe-dependence diagnosis) or 'Mild' (drinking levels and AUDIT scores are well above typical mild/hazardous cutoffs).
article.Age_Median: Table 1 / Results, 'Sample characteristics': overall mean age 27.48 +/- 8.11 years (text: '27.5 +/- 8.1 yrs'), which falls in the <30 bracket.
article.PercentFem: Methods, 'Participants': 90 participants, 55 men and 35 women. 35/90 x 100 = 38.9%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: No race or ethnicity data are reported anywhere in the text (Table 1's baseline variables and the Participants section report only age, sex, smoking status, and drinking/psychometric measures). Coded '.' -- the concept applies to a human sample but was simply not reported.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 0: no income, employment, insurance status, or other SES indicator is reported or discussed anywhere in the article.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: University College London (UCL) and University College Hospital (UCLH), London, United Kingdom -- coded 'NonUS'.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: participants were recruited via open internet advertisements but explicitly excluded if formally diagnosed with or seeking treatment for AUD, and were required to be beer-preferring with a specific hazardous-drinking profile (AUDIT>8, non-SCID-AUD, quantity thresholds). This is a screened, non-treatment-seeking volunteer research sample rather than a real-world clinical/treatment-seeking population; the Discussion itself notes assessment in a treatment-seeking sample 'would have been premature' at this stage.
article.InterventionTherapy: Coded 0: the retrieval procedure (rating/consuming a sample beer or orange juice, then unexpected withholding) is an experimental memory-destabilization manipulation, not therapy, counseling, or a preparation/integration process in the psychedelic-assisted-therapy sense; no counseling or psychotherapeutic component accompanies the ketamine infusion.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 0, consistent with SafetyReported='N'. No AE monitoring protocol, AE form, or safety results are described for this study's participants; Discussion's safety comments ('ketamine is widely used and safe ... its dissociative and psychotogenic properties ... may be contraindicated for certain individuals') are general statements about ketamine's known profile drawn from the wider literature, not a report of what was assessed or observed in this trial's participants.
article.Followup in months: Results, 'Long-term maintenance': drinking levels were compared 'post manipulation (Day 10) across follow-up to 9 months', with explicit 2-week, 3-, 6-, and 9-month assessment points and 9-month respondent Ns reported. Longest reported follow-up = 9 months, measured from Day 10 (post-manipulation/end of the single-session intervention on Day 3), which is the article's own baseline for the follow-up window.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0: the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) appears only in Table 1 as a baseline characteristic with a between-group inferential test at baseline (no significant group difference, p=0.197); no mental-health scale is reported as a pre-post or follow-up outcome anywhere in Results.
article.ReductionMeasured: Coded 1: the primary alcohol-consumption results are framed as a partial, graded reduction in ongoing drinking (e.g., 'a reduction of 23.5 UK units/188g ethanol over a week' in RET+KET; 'halved their average weekly consumption from ~84 to ~41 UK units' by 9 months), not a binary cessation/abstinence outcome.
article.CessationMeasured: Coded 0: no discrete abstinence/complete-cessation rate is reported anywhere; all drinking outcomes (TLFB units, drinking days, binge days) are continuous reduction measures, and participants were explicitly non-treatment-seeking and not pursuing abstinence as a goal.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1: Results, 'Long-term maintenance' explicitly frames the 9-month follow-up as assessing reversion to heavy drinking/rebound -- 'Reversion to heavy drinking typifies drinking interventions. We assessed this by comparing drinking levels post manipulation (Day 10) across follow-up to 9 months' -- and reports 'no evidence of rebound to baseline levels.'
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Coded 1: plasma levels of ketamine and its metabolites (norketamine, dehydroxynorketamine) were measured via gas chromatography as biological/biomarker outcomes (Methods, 'Tasks and apparatus'; Results, 'Predictive blood biomarkers of response').
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'N': the article never describes an adverse-event assessment method (no AE form, no monitoring protocol referenced) and reports no harms results (no AE counts, no statement that no AEs occurred) for the trial's participants. Discussion's remarks on ketamine's tolerability are general, literature-level statements, not a report of what was assessed or found in this study -- per the cardinal rule distinguishing 'no AEs occurred' from 'the authors never looked/reported', this is coded as the latter.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'NA' because SafetyReported='N', per the required NA-only-when-SafetyReported=N rule.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded 'NA' for the same reason as AnyAEReported.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded 'NA' for the same reason as AnyAEReported (the field is Integer/'.'/'NA'; 'NA' applies here since safety was not reported at all, not merely uncounted).
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.', never 'NA' per the field's explicit rule, since no safety assessment was reported for this study.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA': with no AE data reported at all, arm scope for AE values genuinely does not apply.

config_proposal.note: np2=0.14 (F(1,89.17)=19.55, p<0.001) is RET+KET's own reduction in alcohol consumption from baseline to post-manipulation, drawn from a linear mixed model's within-group Time simple effect (Satterthwaite-approximated df), not a classical between-subjects ANOVA or a direct 2-group comparison -- treating this repeated-measures/mixed-model statistic as an input to a between-groups effect-size conversion is the kind of assumption that warrants 'approx' rather than 'clean'. The parallel 3-group Group x Time omnibus interaction on this same outcome was only marginally significant and reported without an eta-squared (F(2,89.432)=3.123, p=0.049), so it could not be used instead; a covariate-adjusted version of that interaction, which the authors explicitly label 'the primary mixed-model analysis of unit alcohol consumption', reports np2=0.078 (F(2,85.42)=3.719, p=0.037) but rests on a post hoc plasma-ketamine covariate outside the original 2x3 design and was not used as the primary value.
